items.stem: Define the term 'fixed costs'.
items.answer: Costs that do not change with the level of output in the short run, such as rent and salaries.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Costs that do not change with the level of output in the short run, such as rent and salaries. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between fixed costs and variable costs.
items.answer: Fixed costs, such as rent, stay the same whatever the output in the short run; variable costs, such as materials, change in proportion to output.
items.markingKey: 1 mark fixed with example; 1 mark variable with example. [2]

items.stem: Explain why it is useful for a business to classify its costs.
items.answer: Knowing which costs are fixed and variable allows it to calculate break-even and contribution, set prices and see how costs change with output.
items.markingKey: 1 mark break-even/contribution; 1 mark pricing/decisions. [2]

items.stem: Based in Doha, Pearl Logistics WLL (private limited company) provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. The business has around 1,500 employees. Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. Explain how Pearl Logistics could use information about its fixed and variable costs.
items.answer: Points to develop for Pearl Logistics: costs can be classified as fixed or variable; calculate break-even output; set prices that cover costs; decide whether to accept extra orders.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: costs can be classified as fixed or variable. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Pearl Logistics (logistics). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. calculate break-even output; set prices that cover costs. [3]

items.answer: Points to develop for Blue Lagoon Tours: costs can be classified as fixed or variable; calculate break-even output; set prices that cover costs; decide whether to accept extra orders.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: costs can be classified as fixed or variable. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Blue Lagoon Tours (tourism). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. calculate break-even output; set prices that cover costs. [3]

items.stem: Based in Chiang Mai, Lotus Spa (sole trader) offers massages and beauty treatments. The business has around 8 employees. The owner wants to introduce online booking and loyalty discounts. Evaluate whether Lotus Spa should try to reduce its fixed costs or its variable costs.
items.answer: For: lower fixed costs reduce break-even; lower variable costs raise contribution per unit; both improve profit. Against: fixed cost cuts may reduce capacity or quality; variable cost cuts may reduce quality; supplier relations. Judgement: for Lotus Spa it depends mainly on its level of output, and also on the structure of its costs.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Lotus Spa: personal services, about 8 employees, sole trader in Thailand; the owner wants to introduce online booking and loyalty discounts). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. lower fixed costs reduce break-even; lower variable costs raise contribution per unit; both improve profit; arguments against, e.g. fixed cost cuts may reduce capacity or quality; variable cost cuts may reduce quality; supplier relations. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on its level of output; the structure of its costs; quality needs. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Lotus Spa. [10]

Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to BatikPay of changing more of its fixed costs into variable costs, e.g. by outsourcing.
items.answer: Advantage: lower break-even output. Disadvantage: higher cost per unit at high output.

items.stem: Define the term 'contribution per unit'.
items.answer: Selling price minus variable cost per unit: the amount each unit contributes to fixed costs and then to profit.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Selling price minus variable cost per unit: the amount each unit contributes to fixed costs and then to profit. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the meaning of contribution.
items.answer: Contribution is selling price minus variable cost; it is what each unit contributes first to covering fixed costs and then to profit.
items.markingKey: 1 mark price − variable cost; 1 mark covers fixed costs then profit. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business would want a large margin of safety.
items.answer: Sales could fall by a large amount before the business makes a loss, so it is less risky.
items.markingKey: 1 mark amount sales can fall; 1 mark lower risk of loss. [2]

items.stem: Demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce. Cape Brew Co. (Pty) Ltd, a private limited company in South Africa with about 140 employees, brews craft beers and low-sugar soft drinks sold through bars and supermarkets. Explain how break-even analysis could help Cape Brew decide whether to launch alcohol-free craft beer.
items.answer: Points to develop for Cape Brew: break-even output = fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit; shows the sales needed to avoid a loss; margin of safety shows risk; tests different prices and costs.

items.stem: Define the term 'break-even chart'.
items.answer: A graph showing fixed costs, total costs and total revenue at different levels of output, with the break-even point where total revenue and total costs cross.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A graph showing fixed costs, total costs and total revenue at different levels of output, with the break-even point where total revenue and total costs cross. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two limitations of break-even analysis.
items.answer: It assumes all output is sold and that the selling price is the same at every level of output; in reality discounts are given and inventory builds up. It also assumes costs are linear.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark limitation, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Explain what happens to a break-even chart if variable cost per unit rises.
items.answer: The total cost line becomes steeper (starting from the same fixed cost), so it crosses total revenue at a higher output: break-even rises and the margin of safety falls.
items.markingKey: 1 mark steeper TC; 1 mark higher break-even. [2]

items.stem: Define the term 'contribution pricing'.
items.answer: Setting a price based on variable cost plus a contribution to fixed costs, often used for special orders when there is spare capacity.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Setting a price based on variable cost plus a contribution to fixed costs, often used for special orders when there is spare capacity. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business might accept an order at a price below its average total cost.
items.answer: If it has spare capacity and fixed costs are already covered, any price above variable cost gives a positive contribution that increases profit.
items.markingKey: 1 mark spare capacity/fixed costs covered; 1 mark positive contribution adds to profit. [2]

items.stem: Explain two ways that cost information helps a business make decisions.
items.answer: It allows prices to be set that cover costs and give a profit; and it shows whether a product or order makes a positive contribution, helping decisions about continuing or accepting it.
